### 1963–1975: Early years and work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sridevi&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 1963–1975: Early years and work")]

Sridevi was born as Shree Amma Yanger Ayyapan[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-Sridevi-15) on 13 August 1963 in [Meenampatti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenampatti "Meenampatti") village[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-:3-16) near [Sivakasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sivakasi "Sivakasi"), [Tamil Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu "Tamil Nadu"), India[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-auto-17) to Ayyapan and Rajeswari.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-hindu-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-week-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-india-20) Her father was a lawyer from Sivakasi while her mother was from [Tirupati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tirupati "Tirupati"), [Andhra Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andhra_Pradesh "Andhra Pradesh").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-22) Sridevi's native language was [Telugu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telugu_language "Telugu language"), and she was fluent in [Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Language "Tamil Language").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-Interview-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-24) She has a sister and two step-brothers.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-25)

> "I lost out on going to school and college life, but I got into the film industry and worked without a gap – from child actor, I went straight to heroine. There was no time to think and I was grateful for it."

—Sridevi, _[The New Indian Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_Indian\_Express "The New Indian Express")_, 2013[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-26)

Sridevi started her career as a child actor at the age of four in the Tamil movie _[Kandhan Karunai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kandhan\_Karunai "Kandhan Karunai")_ in 1967.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-27) Subsequently, she played the role of young [Muruga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muruga "Muruga") in _[Thunaivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thunaivan "Thunaivan")_, which was her first breakthrough as child artist.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-outlookindia.com-28) Actress [Sowcar Janaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sowcar_Janaki "Sowcar Janaki") opined that her "sharp features, sparkling eyes and innocent smile would be more than a handful for the role."[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-ottplay.com-29) Sridevi made her debut in [Telugu cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telugu_cinema "Telugu cinema") as a child artist with the 1970 film _Maa Nanna Nirdoshi_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Baby Sridevi's performance in [_Poompatta_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poompatta_(film) "Poompatta (film)") (1971) in Malayalam won her the [Kerala State Film Award for Best Child Artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Film_Award_for_Best_Child_Artist "Kerala State Film Award for Best Child Artist").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-news15-30)_[Kandhan Karunai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kandhan\_Karunai "Kandhan Karunai")_ (1967), [_Nam Naadu_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nam_Naadu_(1969_film) "Nam Naadu (1969 film)") (1969), _Prarthanai_ (1970), [_Babu_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babu_(1971_film) "Babu (1971 film)") (1971), _[Badi Panthulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badi\_Panthulu "Badi Panthulu")_ (1972), _[Bala Bharatam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bala\_Bharatam "Bala Bharatam")_ (1972), [_Vasantha Maaligai_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasantha_Maligai "Vasantha Maligai") (1972) and _[Bhakta Kumbara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhakta\_Kumbara "Bhakta Kumbara")_ (1974) are the most notable films of her career as a child artist.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-news15-30) In 1972, Sridevi debuted as a child artist in [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") with _[Rani Mera Naam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rani\_Mera\_Naam "Rani Mera Naam")_ directed by [K. S. R. Das](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._S._R._Das "K. S. R. ### 1976–1982: Success in South India

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sridevi&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1976–1982: Success in South India")]

Sridevi's lead roles in [Telugu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telugu_language "Telugu language") include _[Padaharella Vayasu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padaharella\_Vayasu "Padaharella Vayasu")_, _[Konda Veeti Simham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kondaveeti\_Simham "Kondaveeti Simham")_, _[Vetagaadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vetagaadu "Vetagaadu")_, _[Sardar Paparayudu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sardar\_Papa\_Rayudu "Sardar Papa Rayudu")_ and _[Bobbili Puli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobbili\_Puli "Bobbili Puli")_.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-telugu-33) With [Akkineni Nageswara Rao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akkineni_Nageswara_Rao "Akkineni Nageswara Rao"), she appeared in movies such as _[Premabhishekham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premabhishekam\_(1981\_film) "Premabhishekam (1981 film)")_, _[Bangaru Kanuka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangaru\_Kanuka "Bangaru Kanuka")_ and _[Prema Kanuka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prema\_Kanuka "Prema Kanuka")_ as well as with [Krishna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_(Telugu_actor) "Krishna (Telugu actor)") in _[Kalavari Samsaram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalavari\_Samsaram "Kalavari Samsaram")_, _[Adavi Simhalu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adavi\_Simhalu "Adavi Simhalu")_, _[Gharana Donga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gharana\_Donga "Gharana Donga")_, _[Kirayi Kotigadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirayi\_Kotigadu "Kirayi Kotigadu")_, _[Pachani Kapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pachani\_Kapuram "Pachani Kapuram")_, and _[Ram Robert Rahim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram\_Robert\_Rahim "Ram Robert Rahim")_.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-telugu-33) She acted with [Chiranjeevi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiranjeevi "Chiranjeevi") in _[Jagadeka Veerudu Athiloka Sundari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jagadeka\_Veerudu\_Athiloka\_Sundari "Jagadeka Veerudu Athiloka Sundari")_, _[S. P. Parasuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.\_P.\_Parasuram "S. P. Parasuram")_.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-telugu-33) She acted with [Nagarjuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagarjuna_(actor) "Nagarjuna (actor)") in _[Aakhari Poratam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aakhari\_Poratam "Aakhari Poratam")_ (1988), and _[Govinda Govinda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Govinda\_Govinda\_(1994\_film) "Govinda Govinda (1994 film)")_ (1993). ### 1983–1986: Hindi film debut and success

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sridevi&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 1983–1986: Hindi film debut and success")]

Sridevi made her debut as a heroine in Hindi films in _[Solva Sawan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solva\_Sawan "Solva Sawan")_ in 1979.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-45) 4 years later, she was signed to star opposite [Jeetendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeetendra "Jeetendra") in _[Himmatwala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Himmatwala\_(1983\_film) "Himmatwala (1983 film)")_ (remake of Telugu film _[Ooruki Monagadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ooruki\_Monagadu "Ooruki Monagadu")_ (1981)). The film released in 1983, and was one of the highest-grossing Hindi films of the year.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-46) It established Sridevi in Bollywood.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Her dance number "Nainon Mein Sapna" became a rage with _[Rediff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rediff "Rediff")_ stating that "the water pots may have dominated most frames in 'Nainon Mein Sapna', but it was Sridevi's bejewelled outfits and headgears that stole the show".[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-rediff.com-47) She followed with _[Tohfa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tohfa "Tohfa")_, which was the highest-grossing Hindi film of 1984.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-48) The film established Sridevi as one of the leading actresses of Bollywood,[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-Boxofficeindia.com-49) with _[Filmfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare "Filmfare")_ magazine declaring her "Unquestionably #1" on their cover.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The pair of Jeetendra-Sridevi did 16 films together of which _[Himmatwala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Himmatwala\_(1983\_film) "Himmatwala (1983 film)")_ (1983), _[Jaani Dost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaani\_Dost "Jaani Dost")_ (1983), _[Justice Chaudhry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justice\_Chaudhury "Justice Chaudhury")_ (1983), _[Mawaali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mawaali "Mawaali")_ (1983), _Akalmand_ (1984), _[Tohfa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tohfa "Tohfa")_ (1984), _[Balidaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balidaan\_(1985\_film) "Balidaan (1985 film)")_ (1985), _[Aulad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aulad\_(1987\_film) "Aulad (1987 film)")_ (1987), _[Suhaagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suhaagan "Suhaagan")_ (1986), _[Ghar Sansar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghar\_Sansar "Ghar Sansar")_ (1986), _[Dharm Adhikari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharm\_Adhikari "Dharm Adhikari")_ (1986), _[Sone Pe Suhaaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sone\_Pe\_Suhaaga "Sone Pe Suhaaga")_ (1988) were successful, and _[Aag Aur Shola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aag\_Aur\_Shola "Aag Aur Shola")_ (1986), _[Himmat Aur Mehanat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Himmat\_Aur\_Mehanat "Himmat Aur Mehanat")_ (1987), _[Sarfarosh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarfarosh\_(1985\_film) "Sarfarosh (1985 film)")_ (1985) were flops.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-51)

However, it was _[Sadma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sadma "Sadma")_ (1983) which brought Sridevi widespread critical acclaim.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] A remake of her Tamil film _[Moondram Pirai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moondram\_Pirai "Moondram Pirai")_, _Sadma_ is included in _iDiva_'s list of '10 Must Watch Movies That Weren't Blockbusters'.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-idiva.com-52) Sridevi's performance as a child-woman suffering from amnesia was called by _[Indian Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian\_Express "Indian Express")_ "a milestone in her illustrious career".[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-53) Sridevi also featured in the _[Mid-Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mid-Day "Mid-Day")_'s list of 'Challenging Roles played by Bollywood Actors' describing her act in the film as "her best performance ever".[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-54) In 2012, [Adil Hussain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adil_Hussain "Adil Hussain"), Sridevi's co-star in _[English Vinglish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English\_Vinglish "English Vinglish")_ revealed that he became a fan of the actress after watching her in _Sadma_.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-55) The Sridevi-Kamal Hassan pair also appeared on the _[CNN-IBN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN-IBN "CNN-IBN")_ 2012 list of 'Greatest Romantic Couples on Celluloid'.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-56) The film earned Sridevi her first [Filmfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare "Filmfare") nomination for [Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actress "Filmfare Award for Best Actress").

Sridevi had successful pairing with [Rajesh Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Khanna "Rajesh Khanna") in films such as _[Naya Kadam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naya\_Kadam "Naya Kadam")_ (1984), _[Maqsad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maqsad "Maqsad")_ (1984), _[Masterji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masterji "Masterji")_ (1985) and _[Nazrana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazrana\_(1987\_film) "Nazrana (1987 film)")_ (1987). In 1986, came the snake fantasy _[Nagina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagina\_(1986\_film) "Nagina (1986 film)")_ which saw Sridevi play a [shape-shifting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shapeshifting "Shapeshifting") woman. The film turned out to be the second highest-grossing film of the year,[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-57) with _[Box Office India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box\_Office\_India "Box Office India")_ stating that Sridevi remained "the undisputed #1".[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-Boxofficeindia.com-49) It was also named one of the best snake fantasy films by _[Yahoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yahoo "Yahoo")_.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-58)_[Times of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times\_of\_India "Times of India")_ ranked _[Nagina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagina\_(1986\_film) "Nagina (1986 film)")_ as one of the 'Top 10 Snake Films of Hindi Cinema'.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-59) Sridevi's climax dance number "Main Teri Dushman" also remains one of the best snake dances in Bollywood,[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-60) with _Desi Hits_ calling it "one of Sridevi's most iconic dance numbers... that still gives fans goose bumps"[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-61) and _iDiva_ describing it as "the stuff of movie legends".[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-iDiva-62) Nagina is credited as being the film which established Sridevi's position as the biggest female star of the 1980s, rivalling male stars like [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") and [Dharmendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharmendra "Dharmendra"). Besides _[Nagina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagina\_(1986\_film) "Nagina (1986 film)")_, 1986 also saw Sridevi giving box-office hits in [Subhash Ghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subhash_Ghai "Subhash Ghai")'s multi-starrer _[Karma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karma\_(1986\_film) "Karma (1986 film)")_ and [Feroz Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feroz_Khan_(actor) "Feroz Khan (actor)")'s _[Janbaaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janbaaz "Janbaaz")_. According to _[CNN-IBN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN-IBN "CNN-IBN")_'s Bollywood Blockbusters, "Sridevi's popularity grew so much that despite having a guest appearance in _[Janbaaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janbaaz "Janbaaz")_, she completely overshadowed the film's lead heroine [Dimple Kapadia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimple_Kapadia "Dimple Kapadia")."[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-63)

### 1987–1991: Stardom

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sridevi&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 1987–1991: Stardom")]

Sridevi followed the success of _[Nagina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagina "Nagina")_ by playing a goofy crime journalist in the science fiction film _[Mr. India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_India\_(1987\_film) "Mr. India (1987 film)")_ (1987) opposite [Anil Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor "Anil Kapoor"), which was described by _[Rediff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rediff "Rediff")_ as "one of the most iconic films of its time".[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-http-64) Directed by [Shekhar Kapur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur "Shekhar Kapur"), it became one of the highest grossing hits of the year and also found a place in _[Hindustan Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindustan\_Times "Hindustan Times")_' list of 'Top 10 Patriotic Films of Hindi Cinema'.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-66) While the trade famously joked that the film should have been named _Ms. India_,[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]_[Rediff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rediff "Rediff")_ also stated that "Sridevi was a complete show-stealer in the film".[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-http-64) Sridevi's imitation of [Charlie Chaplin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Chaplin "Charlie Chaplin") in the film was described by [_The Times of India_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_of_India "Times of India") as "the most hilarious act she has ever done".[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-67)_Rediff_ also featured Sridevi in its list of 'Super 6 Comic Heroines' stating that "her mobile face expressions could give Jim Carrey sleepless nights" and that "her biggest plus point is her ability to be completely uninhibited in front of the camera".[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-rediff2004-68)

The dance number "Hawaa Hawaai", cited by _The_ _Times of India_ as "one of the unforgettable numbers of Sridevi",[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-69) also became a popular nickname for the actress.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-70) Besides comedy, Sridevi featured in the video for the song "Kaate Nahin Kat Te"; _[Filmfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare "Filmfare")_ described Sridevi as "truly a goddess in a blue sari".[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-72)_Rediff_ also featured the song in its list of 'Top 25 Sari Moments' praising Sridevi's "ability to look erotic even when she's covered from head-to-toe".[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-73) For _Mr. India_, Sridevi commanded ₹1.1 million, making her the highest paid Indian actress. _[Box Office India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box\_Office\_India "Box Office India")_ states that with the success of _Mr. India_, Sridevi "continued her domination" over her contemporaries [Jaya Prada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaya_Prada "Jaya Prada") and [Meenakshi Sheshadri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Sheshadri "Meenakshi Sheshadri").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-Boxofficeindia.com-49)

1989 saw the release of the [Yash Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yash_Chopra "Yash Chopra")'s romantic musical saga _[Chandni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chandni\_(1989\_film) "Chandni (1989 film)")_, with Sridevi playing the title role. The film emerged as one of the biggest blockbusters of 1989.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-74) Cited by _The Times of India_ as "one of the most watched films of Indian cinema",[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-75) the film also reaffirmed Sridevi's position as the top female star of the 1980s.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-77) She was also paid ₹1.5 million for the lead role.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-indianexpress.com-78) While she topped the _[Hindustan Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindustan\_Times "Hindustan Times")_' list of Yash Chopra's 'Top 5 Heroines',[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-Hindustan_Times-79)_[CNN-IBN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN-IBN "CNN-IBN")_ also ranked her first on a similar list, saying "Yash Chopra immortalized Sridevi as the perfect Chandni".[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-80)_[India Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India\_Today "India Today")_ and _[NDTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NDTV "NDTV")_ also included her in such lists, stating that the film established Sridevi "as the nation's sweetheart".[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-83)_[The Tribune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Tribune\_(Chandigarh) "The Tribune (Chandigarh)")_ wrote: "Leena Daru scored a winner again when she created the 'Chandni Look' for Sridevi. Every street corner sold the salwar-kameez and dupatta that gave the heroine a refreshingly understated look, rarely seen on the Indian screen",[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-84) Sridevi's dance number "Mere Haathon Mein Nau Nau Choodiyaan" proved also popular with audiences,[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-85) and she also lent her voice to the film's popular title-track.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-86)

The same year, Sridevi also starred in the [slapstick comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slapstick_film "Slapstick film")_[ChaalBaaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChaalBaaz "ChaalBaaz")_, which had her play a double role of twin sisters separated at birth. _Filmfare_ ranked her performance #4 in its list of '80 Iconic Performances of Hindi Cinema', stating that "Sridevi's penchant for giggles and her ability to look distinctly tearful when required polishes these performances to perfection. Hell, she made Sunny Deol and Rajinikanth look like sidekicks in the film".[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-87)_The_ _Times of India_ article 'Bollywood's Hit Double Roles' wrote, "Sridevi's performance had rocked the box office".[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-88)_Rediff_ featured the film in its countdown of "25 Best Double Roles in Bollywood" saying "What you don't realise until you have seen _Chaalbaaz_ is just how incredible Sridevi is at depicting both ends of the spectrum",[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-89) and that the film "cemented her position as an actress with a killer comic timing".[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-http-64) Speaking to [_The Indian Express_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Express "Indian Express") about Sridevi's act in _ChaalBaaz_, the director [Pankaj Parashar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pankaj_Parashar "Pankaj Parashar") said "She proved her range with the movie and after that she got lots of offers which saw her in a double role".[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-90) Her slapstick rain dance "Na Jaane Kahaan Se Aayi Hai" became successful with _The Times of India_ describing it as "a Sridevi classic where she simply looked wow with her chirpy expressions and rain drops kissing her cheeks."[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-91) Sridevi garnered [Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actress "Filmfare Award for Best Actress") nominations at Filmfare for both _Chandni_ and _ChaalBaaz_ in 1989, winning for the latter.

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/42/Madhuri_%26_Sridevi.jpg/250px-Madhuri_%26_Sridevi.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Madhuri_&_Sridevi.jpg)

Sridevi (right) with actress [Madhuri Dixit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhuri_Dixit "Madhuri Dixit") on season 5 of _[Jhalak Dikhhla Jaa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jhalak\_Dikhhla\_Jaa\_season\_5 "Jhalak Dikhhla Jaa season 5")_ (2012)

Chopra then cast Sridevi in his 1991 intergenerational musical romantic drama _[Lamhe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamhe "Lamhe")_. _The Times of India_ included it in its list of 'Top 10 Films of Yash Chopra' describing it as a tale of "love transcending the boundaries of time and space"[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-92) while _[Rediff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rediff "Rediff")_ called it "Quite easily one of his most definitive films, Chopra surpassed his own findings of romance with the insightful, lovely _Lamhe._"[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-rediff2-93) Sridevi played both the roles of mother and daughter in what _iDiva_ described as "another double role but it was unlike any played before."[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-iDiva-62) Hailed by _[Rediff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rediff "Rediff")_ as "one of the most remarkable films of her career... often considered a film way ahead of its time",[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-http-64)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-94) Sridevi's folk dance number 'Morni Baga Ma' also became a rage and was placed among the 'Top 5 Songs' of Yash Chopra by _[Hindustan Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindustan\_Times "Hindustan Times")_.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-Hindustan_Times-79)_Lamhe_ was an underwhelming success at the box-office, but received widespread critical acclaim and has become a cult classic over the years.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-idiva.com-52)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-95) Talking about the film, critic Rachel Dwyer wrote in her biography of the film-maker "Chopra's own favourite film, _Lamhe_ (_Moments_ (1991)), divided the audience on a class basis: it was hugely popular with metropolitan elites and the overseas market, which allowed it to break even, but it had a poor box-office response (largely lower-class, especially the repeat audience) because of its supposed incest theme".[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-96)_[The Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hindu "The Hindu")_ reported that "With shades of incest, _Lamhe_ caused more than a flutter and remained the talk of the town",[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-97) while Sridevi herself admitted in an interview with [Rajeev Masand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajeev_Masand "Rajeev Masand") that she found the subject "too bold".[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-98) Though the film flopped at the box-office, with _[Rediff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rediff "Rediff")_ describing its failure as "one of those bizarre, unexplained moments of cinema",[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-rediff2-93)_Lamhe_ picked up 5 Filmfare trophies including [Best Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Film "Filmfare Award for Best Film") and a second [Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actress "Filmfare Award for Best Actress") trophy for Sridevi. Her popular Rajasthani costumes in the film also won designer [Neeta Lulla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neeta_Lulla "Neeta Lulla") her first [National Film Award for Best Costume Design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Costume_Design "National Film Award for Best Costume Design").[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-99)

### 1992–1997: Continued success

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sridevi&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 1992–1997: Continued success")]

In 1992, Sridevi starred in the epic drama _[Khuda Gawah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khuda\_Gawah "Khuda Gawah")_ opposite [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan"). The actress played a double role again as an [Afghan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghans "Afghans") warrior Benazir and her daughter Mehndi. Shot mostly in [Mazar-i-Sharif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazar-i-Sharif "Mazar-i-Sharif"), Afghanistan,[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-ndtv.com-100) it did good business with _[BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC")_ reporting that "it ran to packed houses for 10 weeks in [Kabul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabul "Kabul")". _Khuda Gawah_ still remains popular in Afghanistan and _[Rediff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rediff "Rediff")_ reported that the film is "in great demand after the reopening of cinema halls in the country" in 2001.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-101) For Khuda Gawah, Sridevi earned ₹2.5 million for the role.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-indianexpress.com-78) At Filmfare, the film picked up the [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Director "Filmfare Award for Best Director") trophy, while Sridevi earned a nomination for Best Actress. During the production of [_Jurassic Park_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic_Park_(film) "Jurassic Park (film)") in 1992–93, acclaimed Hollywood director and producer [Steven Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg") approached Sridevi for a small role in the film. However, Sridevi, after evaluating the stature of the role, refused the offer.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-102)

Sridevi's big-budget 1993 release _[Roop Ki Rani Choron Ka Raja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roop\_Ki\_Rani\_Choron\_Ka\_Raja "Roop Ki Rani Choron Ka Raja")_ was one of India's most expensive films ever made.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-103) Though the film failed at the box office, Sridevi was appreciated with _[Times of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times\_of\_India "Times of India")_ calling her disguise in a comedy scene "the best ever South Indian role played by any actress".[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-timesofindia.indiatimes.com-104) She next starred in the 1993 thriller _[Gumrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gumrah\_(1993\_film) "Gumrah (1993 film)")_, opposite [Sanjay Dutt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjay_Dutt "Sanjay Dutt"). Directed by [Mahesh Bhatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahesh_Bhatt "Mahesh Bhatt"), the actress played a singer falsely accused of drugs smuggling in [Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong "Hong Kong"). _Bollyspice_ stated in its 'Sridevi Retrospective' that "Despite great performances from the rest of the cast, _Gumrah_ was really Sridevi's film. She managed to exemplify female emotion and robustness to a great degree that you remember the film largely for her significant contribution towards it,"[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-bollyspice-105) Her performance earned her another nomination for Best Actress at Filmfare.

In 1994, Sridevi teamed up with [Anil Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor "Anil Kapoor") again in _[Laadla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laadla\_(1994\_film) "Laadla (1994 film)")_ playing business tycoon Sheetal Jaitley. The character, described by _[Times of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times\_of\_India "Times of India")_ as "rude, dominant and very competitive"[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-timesofindia.indiatimes.com-104) brought her yet another Best Actress nomination at Filmfare. She acted in her comeback film in Malayalam in 1996 – [Bharathan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharathan "Bharathan")'s _[Devaraagam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devaraagam "Devaraagam")_, a love story in which she starred opposite [Aravind Swamy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aravind_Swamy "Aravind Swamy").

The last major film Sridevi starred in before she took a break from the industry was the romantic drama _[Judaai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judaai\_(1997\_film) "Judaai (1997 film)")_, released in 1997. Along with [Anil Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor "Anil Kapoor") and [Urmila Matondkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar "Urmila Matondkar"), the actress played a greedy housewife going to extreme lengths for money. Talking about her swan-song, critic Subhash K. Jha wrote that Sridevi "left us with the most stunning hurrah in _Judaai_. A terrible film that I've watched countless times to see her play the money-minded harridan who 'sells' her husband to Urmila Matondkar. Who but Sridevi could carry of such an outrageous role with such enthusiastic élan?!"[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-106) while _Bollyspice_ stated that "She used her polished acting skills to illustrate her character's greed and individualism at such a grotesque level."[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-http-64)_Judaai_ earned Sridevi her eighth Best Actress nomination at Filmfare. In 1996, Sridevi married Boney Kapoor of the famed Bollywood royalty, the Kapoor family. During the years 1996–97, her mother was suffering from brain cancer-induced complications. After her mother's death in 1997, Sridevi went on a hiatus from the film industry.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-107)

### 2004–2018: Comeback, television debut and final roles

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sridevi&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2004–2018: Comeback, television debut and final roles")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/64/English_Vinglish_shooting_03.jpg/250px-English_Vinglish_shooting_03.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:English_Vinglish_shooting_03.jpg)

Sridevi with [Ajith Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ajith_Kumar "Ajith Kumar") on the sets of film _[English Vinglish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English\_Vinglish "English Vinglish")_ in 2012

After a 6-year hiatus, Sridevi briefly returned to the small screen in the Sahara sitcom _[Malini Iyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malini\_Iyer "Malini Iyer")_ (2004–2005). She also appeared on _[Jeena Isi Ka Naam Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeena\_Isi\_Ka\_Naam\_Hai "Jeena Isi Ka Naam Hai")_ (2004) and as a judge in the TV show _Kaboom_ (2005).[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-108) She performed a medley of some of her musical numbers at the [52nd Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/52nd_Filmfare_Awards "52nd Filmfare Awards") in 2007. She was also a member of the board of directors at the Asian Academy of Film & Television.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-109)

On 19 September 2009, Sridevi appeared on the [Sony TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Entertainment_Television "Sony Entertainment Television") show _[10 Ka Dum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10\_Ka\_Dum "10 Ka Dum")_. On 13 May 2012, Sridevi appeared on the [Star Plus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/StarPlus "StarPlus") talk-show _[Satyamev Jayate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satyamev\_Jayate\_(talk\_show) "Satyamev Jayate (talk show)")_.

Sridevi had also developed a passion for painting. In March 2010, her paintings were sold by an international art auction house with the money raised being donated.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-110)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Sridevi07.jpg/250px-Sridevi07.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sridevi07.jpg)

Sridevi at the premiere of _English Vinglish_ in 2012

After a 15-year absence from film, Sridevi starred in _[English Vinglish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English\_Vinglish "English Vinglish")_ (2012), a comedy-drama helmed by debutante director [Gauri Shinde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauri_Shinde "Gauri Shinde").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-111) In the film, she played Shashi Godbole, a housewife who enrolls in an English-speaking course after her husband and daughter's mocking of her English skills. The film and Sridevi's performance received widespread critical acclaim. _[The Times of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Times\_of\_India "The Times of India")_ called it "easily one of the best films of 2012!" and Sridevi's performance "a masterclass for actors."[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-112) Raja Sen of _[Rediff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rediff "Rediff")_ found the film "a winner all the way [...] Sridevi excels in fleshing out her character",[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-rediff-113) and critic Subhash K. Jha said Sridevi "makes the contemporary actresses, even the coolest ones, look like jokes... If you watch only 2 films every year make sure you see _English Vinglish_ twice!"[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-114)[Rajeev Masand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajeev_Masand "Rajeev Masand") of _[CNN-IBN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN-IBN "CNN-IBN")_ wrote Sridevi delivers "a performance that is nothing short of perfect [...] It's warm and fuzzy, and leaves you with a big smile on your face."[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-115) "Sridevi doesn't miss a beat. Her performance is a triumph!", added the critic [Anupama Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupama_Chopra "Anupama Chopra").[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-116)[Komal Nahta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Komal_Nahta "Komal Nahta") said she "makes the best comeback in Bollywood history and delivers a landmark performance."[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-117)

With the high critical acclaim and massive commercial success of _English Vinglish_, Sridevi became the only actress in Bollywood to make a successful comeback as a leading lady after marriage and a long hiatus.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-Indiawest-118)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-119) Gauri Shinde featured her in the _Financial Times_ 2012 list of '25 Indians To Watch'.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-120) She topped _Rediff.com_'s annual listing of the "Bollywood's Best Actresses" in 2012; the website wrote _English Vinglish_ "is a simple film where things are credible, never melodramatic" and Sridevi "always judges the tone right. It's the sort of performance younger actresses should learn from."[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-121) Sridevi was declared the most-admired Bollywood actress of 2012 in a mobile survey conducted by _Vuclip_, the world's largest mobile research company.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-122) She was nominated for several awards, including her ninth nomination for Best Actress at Filmfare.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-Filmfare_nom_EV-123) Following an appearance during the song "Apna Bombay Talkies" in the film _[Bombay Talkies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay\_Talkies\_(film) "Bombay Talkies (film)")_ (2013),[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-124) Sridevi starred in the Tamil fantasy action adventure film _[Puli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puli\_(2015\_film) "Puli (2015 film)")_ (2015),[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-125) which became her last Tamil film before her death in 2018.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-126)

[![Image 9](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/77/Sridevi_January_2018.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sridevi_January_2018.jpg)

Sridevi at the HT Style Awards in January 2018

Sridevi was next seen in her home production titled _[Mom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mom\_(film) "Mom (film)")_ (2017), which marked her 300th film.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-127) In the psychological thriller film, she played a mother who sets out to avenge the rape of her daughter. Sridevi said that as a mother and an artiste, she empathised with her character's rage, and found it hard to be in a normal state during the filming.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-128)_Mom_ was released on 7 July 2017 to highly positive reviews, with critics widely appreciating Sridevi's performance.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-129)_The Times of India_ and _The Indian Express_ added Sridevi "demonstrates why she is the high-priestess of Indian cinema" and that she "needs only a twitch or a glance to prove that she is a powerhouse and there are several scenes she lifts by just being there."[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-130)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-Shubhra_Gupta-131) For her performance, Sridevi received the [National Film Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Actress "National Film Award for Best Actress") and earned nominations for [Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actress "Filmfare Award for Best Actress") and [Best Actress (Critics)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Critics_Award_for_Best_Actress "Filmfare Critics Award for Best Actress") at Filmfare and the [Screen Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Award_for_Best_Actress "Screen Award for Best Actress").[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-132) At the time of her death, Sridevi was not shooting for any upcoming films and her last on-screen appearance was in [Aanand L. Rai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aanand_L._Rai "Aanand L. Rai")'s film _[Zero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero\_(2018\_film) "Zero (2018 film)")_ (2018) in a cameo.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-133) Sridevi had signed the 2019 period romantic drama _[Kalank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalank "Kalank")_, produced by [Karan Johar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karan_Johar "Karan Johar"); however, due to her demise she was replaced by [Madhuri Dixit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhuri_Dixit "Madhuri Dixit").[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-134) Another film she had signed, was to play a cameo role in the [Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam_cinema "Malayalam cinema") film _Sree Sree Devaraagam_, a sequel to Sridevi's own 1996 film _[Devaraagam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devaraagam "Devaraagam")_, was subsequently shelved after her death in 2018.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-135)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sridevi&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Sridevi was always accompanied by her mother Rajeswari or by her sister Srilatha to the film sets during shooting of her films between 1972 and 1994.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-136) The politician [Sanjay Ramasamy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjay_Ramasamy "Sanjay Ramasamy") has been married to her sister Srilatha since 1989.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-137)

Sridevi campaigned for her father when he contested the [Sivakasi constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sivakasi_(state_assembly_constituency) "Sivakasi (state assembly constituency)") in [1989 assembly elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_Tamil_Nadu_Legislative_Assembly_election "1989 Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly election"), but eventually lost in the elections.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-:3-16) Her father died in 1990 of heart attack, while she was shooting for _Lamhe_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-:3-16)[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-138) Her mother died in 1996,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-:3-16) as a result of the complications suffered from an operation that she underwent in 1995 on a brain tumour at [Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memorial_Sloan_Kettering_Cancer_Center "Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center") in New York. The neurosurgeon operated on the wrong side of her brain destroying her vital tissues of vision and recent memory. This was widely reported in US media at that time which then led to a successful court battle and prompted then President [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton")'s proposal of a program for hospitals to disclose their medical errors.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-139)[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-140)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-141)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-142)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/Sridevi%2C_Boney_Kapoor_at_Esha_Deol%27s_wedding_reception_02.jpg/250px-Sridevi%2C_Boney_Kapoor_at_Esha_Deol%27s_wedding_reception_02.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sridevi,_Boney_Kapoor_at_Esha_Deol's_wedding_reception_02.jpg)

Sridevi with her husband Boney Kapoor at [Esha Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esha_Deol "Esha Deol")'s wedding reception in 2011

Sridevi was extremely discreet about her privacy and rarely gave interviews or discussed her private life in them.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-Guardian-4) In 1996, she married producer [Boney Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boney_Kapoor "Boney Kapoor"). Their children are [Janhvi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janhvi_Kapoor "Janhvi Kapoor") (born 1997), and [Khushi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khushi_Kapoor "Khushi Kapoor") (born 2000), both film actresses.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-143)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-144)

Despite being known for her portrayals of a strong, vivacious and exuberant woman on-screen, Sridevi was an extremely introverted and reserved person off-screen. _[CNN-IBN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN-IBN "CNN-IBN")_ correspondent [Rajeev Masand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajeev_Masand "Rajeev Masand") says; "I have never known anyone who was so painfully shy, so quiet off-screen, who just transformed into a force of nature when the cameras came on. She was an interviewer's nightmare, but the movie-buff's dream".[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-Twitter-145) Commenting on her reserved nature, _[Firstpost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firstpost "Firstpost")_ says; "Behind the glamorous heroine with twinkling, magical eyes and a stunning face, was an inherently shy woman, often mistaken as arrogant. The truth is she was shy. Having begun to act when she was just 4, she did not complete formal education or get much of a chance to interact with kids of her own age. Consequently, she developed a strong dislike for crowds and noise."[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-Firstpost-146)

Boney Kapoor shared that Sridevi didn't speak to him for six months after he proposed, as he was married with two kids at the time. Despite the initial rejection, he eventually convinced her, and they married soon after.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-:4-147)

## Death and funeral

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sridevi&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Death and funeral")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3c/Sridevi_funeral_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Sridevi_funeral_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sridevi_funeral_(cropped).jpg)

Mortal remains of Sridevi lying in a casket during funeral procession in February 2018

On 20 February 2018, Sridevi and her younger daughter Khushi had flown to [Al Jazirah Al Hamra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Jazirah_Al_Hamra "Al Jazirah Al Hamra") in [Ras Al Khaimah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al_Khaimah "Ras Al Khaimah"), [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates"), to attend the wedding of her husband's nephew Mohit Marwah. She decided to spend a couple of days in [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai "Dubai") to shop for her elder daughter Janhvi's 21st birthday, after the wedding.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-148)[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-149) Her husband Boney Kapoor was not present with them on the wedding day, as he had to attend a meeting in [Lucknow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucknow "Lucknow") on 22 February. However, he had already planned a surprise visit to his wife, with whom he spoke on the morning of 24 February, when she told him that "Papa (that's how Sridevi addressed Boney), I'm missing you."[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-150) According to Boney, he took a 15:30 flight to Dubai and reached [Jumeirah Emirates Towers Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jumeirah_Emirates_Towers_Hotel "Jumeirah Emirates Towers Hotel") around 18:20 in Room 2201 where Sridevi was staying. She and Boney briefly met, chatted for 30 minutes or so and decided to have dinner.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-151) Sridevi went to bathe and get dressed for dinner, while Boney waited in the living room. After 15–20 minutes, around 19:00, he called out to her as they were getting late but did not get a response.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-152)

Sridevi was pronounced dead on 24 February 2018 at 19:00 [GMT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenwich_Mean_Time "Greenwich Mean Time") in her hotel room where her husband had found her.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-Hotel-1)[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-:2-153) At first, it was announced by her brother in-law [Sanjay Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjay_Kapoor "Sanjay Kapoor") to the Indian media that the cause of death was a [cardiac arrest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_arrest "Cardiac arrest"), but an investigation into her death began early Sunday morning around 2:30, and the case was transferred to Dubai Public Prosecution by [Dubai Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai_Police_Force "Dubai Police Force"), where General Department of Forensic Evidence, Dubai revealed that the cause of death was "accidental [drowning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drowning "Drowning")".[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-154) The [toxicology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toxicology "Toxicology") report later also revealed that traces of alcohol were found in her body, and water was found in her lungs.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-155)

After rumours that news of her death was an [Internet hoax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_hoax "Internet hoax"), Sanjay Kapoor confirmed her death.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-156) Her fans, co-stars and other Bollywood stars posted condolences on [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") to mourn the death.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-:2-153)[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-157) After a few days of police investigation, on 27 February, Sridevi's case was closed, and on the night of that day, her body was flown back to [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai"), India. Ashraf Thamarassery helped bring back her body to India[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-158)[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-159) by her husband and her stepson, [Arjun Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjun_Kapoor "Arjun Kapoor"), on a private jet belonging to [Anil Ambani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Ambani "Anil Ambani").[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-160) Her funeral took place on 28 February, at the [Vile Parle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vile_Parle "Vile Parle") Seva Samaj [Crematorium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crematorium "Crematorium") in Mumbai. The final rites were performed by her husband Boney Kapoor.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-Cremation-161)[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-162) Sridevi was cremated with state honours and also received a gun salute at her funeral.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-163) Her pyre was lit by her husband.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-164) On 3 March, Sridevi's ashes were flown into [Tamil Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu "Tamil Nadu") via [Chennai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai "Chennai") by her husband and her two daughters Janhvi Kapoor and Khushi Kapoor and later taken to and immersed in the sea off the coast of [Rameswaram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rameswaram "Rameswaram").[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-Ashes_Burial-165)[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-166)

### Tributes and reactions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sridevi&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Tributes and reactions")]

The film industry, friends, and fans responded to her death through social and other media outlets. Her husband, Boney Kapoor, wrote: "To the world, she was their _Chandni_, the actor par excellence, their Sridevi, but to me, she was my love, my friend, mother to our girls, my partner. To our daughters, she was their everything, their life. She was the axis around which our family ran."[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-167) The Prime Minister of India, [Narendra Modi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narendra_Modi "Narendra Modi") lamented the death of Sridevi. On social media, he stated: "Saddened by the untimely demise of noted actor Sridevi. She was a veteran of the film industry, whose long career included diverse roles and memorable performances. My thoughts are with her family and admirers in this hour of grief. May her soul rest in peace."[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-168) President [Ram Nath Kovind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram_Nath_Kovind "Ram Nath Kovind") wrote: "Shocked to hear of passing of movie star Sridevi. She has left millions of fans heartbroken. Her performances in films such as _Moondram Pirai_, _Lamhe_ and _English Vinglish_ remain an inspiration for other actors. My condolences to her family and close associates."[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-169)

Many from the film community and Sridevi's close relatives paid homage to her at Celebration Sports Club in [Lokhandwala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lokhandwala_Complex "Lokhandwala Complex") and at her funeral.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-170)[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-171)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-172) Thousands of fans took to streets to pay their respects. Police had to resort to lathi-charge to control the fans who gathered for the procession from Celebration Sports Complex to the crematorium. The crowd was said to number more than 7,000.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-173)

Sridevi's funeral is estimated to have attracted the fourth-highest number of mourners, ranking below the three previous biggest funeral processions of non-political film personalities [Kishore Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kishore_Kumar "Kishore Kumar"), [Mohammed Rafi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammed_Rafi "Mohammed Rafi") and [Rajesh Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Khanna "Rajesh Khanna") in India from the Hindi film industry.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-174)

## Legacy and influence

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sridevi&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Legacy and influence")]

Sridevi is highly regarded for her range as an actor, critics have commended, particularly her comedic abilities[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-rediff2004-68) and her skills as a dancer.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-175) During the 1980s, Sridevi was the highest-earning woman in the Indian entertainment industry.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-Boxofficeindia.com-49) For her role in _[Mr. India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_India\_(1987\_film) "Mr. India (1987 film)")_ (1987), she was paid a then-unprecedented ₹11 lakhs (equivalent to ₹138 lakhs in 2023; ~US$1,820,000 in 2025), making her the highest-paid Indian actress ever when adjusted for inflation.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-176) In a 2013 national poll conducted by _[CNN-IBN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN-IBN "CNN-IBN")_ on the occasion of the centenary of Indian cinema, Sridevi was voted "India's Greatest Actress in 100 Years",[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-177)[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-178) and she placed #10 in a UK poll, "100 Greatest Bollywood Stars", in the same year.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-179) In 2012, Sridevi was placed at No. 2 by _NDTV_ in the listing of "The most popular Bollywood actresses of all time".[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-180) Sridevi featured in Box Office India's _Top Actresses_ list from 1983 to 1993 and topped of the list five times (1987 to 1991).[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-181)

An epitaph in _[Firstpost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firstpost "Firstpost")_ pointed out that Sridevi had been sufficiently important as an actor to be able to refuse parts in movies,[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-182) and _[The News Minute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_News\_Minute "The News Minute")_ called her "a pathbreaker in many ways".[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-183)_[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ called her "the undisputed queen of Indian Cinema".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-Guardian-4)

> "If Sridevi had no other identity beyond the films that she did, the audiences probably have no concept of films in India without her. Irrespective of the era you were born in or the actors you liked, the cosmos of Hindi film fans is divided into two distinctive groups of those like Sridevi and the others. Unlike most other iconic stars that, in a way, took over from their predecessors, Sridevi never really replaced anyone and perhaps it is this aspect that makes her unique and peerless."

—_[Firstpost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firstpost "Firstpost")_ on the influence of Sridevi.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-184)[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-FOOTNOTELongworth20137-185)

Film critic [Sukanya Verma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sukanya_Verma "Sukanya Verma") described Sridevi as "one-of-a-kind". She wrote, "Sridevi's biggest plus point is her ability to be completely uninhibited in front of the camera."[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-rediff2004-68) Sridevi is cited by media publications as a fashion icon. Her taste in clothes was varied and ranged from stylish casual to opulently majestic. She made her debut as a [fashion model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fashion_model "Fashion model") in 2008. The actress modelled clothes for designers Priya and Chintan at the [Lakme Fashion Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakme_Fashion_Week "Lakme Fashion Week").[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-186) The next year, she displayed the work of jewellery designer Queenie Dhodhy at the HDIL India Couture Week.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-187) She worked at Lakme Fashion Week again in 2010,[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] and at Delhi Couture Week 2012, showing clothes designed by [Sabyasachi Mukherjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabyasachi_Mukherjee "Sabyasachi Mukherjee").[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-188)

She has also appeared on the cover of several fashion magazines. In 2007, she was featured on the cover of _Hi Blitz_ with the tagline "The Goddess Returns".[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-189) In 2011, she featured on the cover of _[Marie Claire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie\_Claire "Marie Claire")_,[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] and in 2012, she was on the cover of _[L'Officiel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L'Officiel "L'Officiel")_.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-190) In 2013, Sridevi appeared on the cover of _[Vogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vogue\_(magazine) "Vogue (magazine)")_, which was mentioned in _[Hindustan Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindustan\_Times "Hindustan Times")_,[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-191)_[The Times of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Times\_of\_India "The Times of India")_,[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-192) and _[India Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India\_Today "India Today")_.[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-193)

Sridevi received the 'Ultimate Diva' award at the Ciroc Filmfare Glamour & Style Awards in 2015.[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-194)

Sridevi's performances, acting style and technique have been influential and have inspired numerous actresses including [Divya Bharti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divya_Bharti "Divya Bharti"),[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi#cite_note-195)[Juhi Chawla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juhi_Chawla "Juhi Where your donation goes

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://wikimediafoundation.org/annualreports/current/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

32% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

11% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

Where your donation goes

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://wikimediafoundation.org/annualreports/current/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

32% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

11% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.
